utterances.text: How long was that conversation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: She just asked me whether I would be prepared to testify, I said I would, and this is what it all boiled down to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was before or after you talked to the Prosecutor's investigator?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was before I came here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Was it before or after February 1996, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What do you mean, the conversation with whom? In February 1996, I went to Timosvara to give a statement there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is right. Was this conversation with this woman before or after you went to Timosvara?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I spoke to that woman, I got in touch with her just before I came here, maybe it was in May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You called her or she called you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: She called me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You talked to her about what your testimony and the facts were going to be, what you knew about the case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did she tell you what any of the other witnesses had said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did she help prepare you for your testimony, telling you what kinds of questions may be asked or what the courtroom looks like or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nothing. She did not tell me anything. We just spoke on the phone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the conversation about "I am going to go to The Hague" or "I want you to go to The Hague and here is where your plane tickets will be", or did you talk about the substance of your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nothing, she just told me where to pick up my ticket and how to get here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: She told you that back in May of this year, about four months ago?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You did not talk to anyone about this case between that conversation with this woman back in May and your conversation with Mr. Turone after you got to The Hague; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let us step back. Before that conversation with this woman back in May, did you have any other conversations with anyone about your testimony here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How about an investigator for the Office of the Prosecutor over in Timosvara, over in Romania. Did you have a conversation with that person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you never talked to --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Excuse me, who did I talk to?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: An investigator for the Office of the Prosecutor, a man whose name looks like he is an oriental man?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Timosvara, I did talk to him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Let me step back to that woman. Where was she calling you from, do you know, that woman you had the conversation with?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, so she is -- does the phrase Serbian Woman's Congress mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have never heard of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, that is fine. How long was the conversation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean on the phone?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you meet her in person and talk to her on the telephone, or did you just talk to her on the phone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I just talked to her on the phone. I do not know that woman. We just spoke on the phone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how she found out who you are and where you are?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: She heard about me because this tragedy happened to me, this is what I stated in Timosvara. If possible I wanted to talk about that, I wanted to say about my family, because my neighbours killed my sister-in-law, my wife and my father and I had been through many things and that is why she called me to come here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. What I am trying to get at, sir, is, until I saw your name on a witness list, I did not know you existed. How did she know that you existed, that you even knew anything about this case? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Probably she had to know about me because I had given a statement in Timosvara.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did she indicate to you that she knew what was in your statement that you gave at Timosvara?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, she did not say that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When she was talking, did it sound like she knew what was in your statement in Timosvara?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have no idea. She probably knew, but she did not say anything to me, she just told me how to come here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did you have any conversations other than with Mr. Fujiwara and Ms. Vokmen, I believe it is (redacted)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: (redacted) Did you have any other conversations with anybody about your testimony here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you were invited to Timosvara by somebody. I am sure you did not just go vacationing in Romania?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was invited by Dordic, Milica Dordic, whatever her name was, in Belgrade to go to Timosvara to give a statement there. Dordic Mila, that was her name. Maybe you are familiar with that name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Is she involved with the Association of Detainees, do you know, in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: She probably does work for them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did you talk to her about what you know about this case, or anybody from her organisation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We talked and she also went with us to Timosvara and she said "tell them everything you know, everything you have seen. Do not tell them anything else".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you give her a statement, a written statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Timosvara?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, the woman from Belgrade. Did you give her a written statement before you went to Timosvara?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you talk to her after you gave the statement to Mr. Fujiwara at Timosvara about the contents of your statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not even see her.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did she tell you how the Association of Detainees knew who you are or where you were, since you are not a member of that organisation? Did she tell you how they found you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was all through friends, because we all mostly knew about each other, where people were. I told them about somebody and then somebody told them about me and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Was there anybody before that that you talked to about your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, looking at the clock, it is 12.57. I think I am done, but I would sure appreciate if we broke early and let me think about it over the lunch break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You are still hanging on until we resume at 2.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. I may very well just pass the witness, but if you could give me the lunch break to think about it, I would appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, I think we will break now, if you are continuing, you might continue after we resume.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. I appreciate that very much. Thank you very much, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber will have a break now and resume at 2.30. (1.00 pm) (Adjourned until 2.30 pm) 20 21 22 23 24 25 (2.30 pm)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Moran.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Good afternoon again, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I hope you had a good lunch and feel a little relaxed. I think I will be fairly short with you and we will get you back about the rest of your life. Let me jump to another topic, one we have not talked about.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That incident you described with the two brothers having performed oral sex acts on each other.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in the hangar, Zenga and Delic came and then these two Dordic brothers, Zenga was beating them and Delic was sitting there watching. Then Zenga in front of all of us forced the two brothers to -- I do not know how to put it, their sex organs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am not asking you in that kind of detail. What I am going to ask you is this, sir. Vaso Dordic testified about this also in open session in the same chair you are sitting in. His testimony about that is on pages 4360 and 4361 of the transcript, okay? In that testimony, he never mentioned that Mr. Delic was there or involved with it in any way. My question to you is, sir --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was there, I know that and I am certain about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Mr. Djordjic just did not notice it, is that your position, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe he did not notice that in his fear, but I know that, I saw it with my own eyes. I was there and I would not have said it unless I had seen it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, sir. If you would like, I could read or have read to you or give you in English, I am afraid I do not have a Serbian transcript, copies of exactly what Mr. Dordic testified to here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know, to be honest. The only thing I am interested in is what I have seen myself and that is what I am saying here, only the truth. I am not interested in anything else. Maybe he did not notice that, but I did see it and I would not have said it unless I had seen it myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, sir. So Mr. Djordjic did not notice everything while this was occurring?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Objection, your Honour. Asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Okay, fine. Let us go on to another subject, sir. Slobodan Zelenovic; do you know him, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I know him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he have a weapon, sir? If so, what kind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think he had a M48 rifle, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The same kind that you had.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if he used it at all, if he discharged that weapon, fired it at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not think so. As far as I know, he did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, you were released directly from the Celebici camp; is that not right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know whether Mr. Delic helped arrange for your release?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well I do not know. As I said, Delic only hit me once, he left me alone. On that day, 31st August 1992, at the end of the day, he came, he went from one to the other in the hangar, he reached me. I got up and I said, "yes, Mr. Commander" and he said, "let me see your category". He looked at a list and then he told me, he whispered to me, "you are going home tonight". That is what happened. Towards the end of the day or evening, it was about 10.00 in the evening, they came to pick us up in a van and they wrote down on a certificate that they were releasing us to go home. We had freedom of movement only within the village. Then they drove us to Podorasac, there were I do not know how many people, 20, I do not know and we went back to our homes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, is it not true that the word in your village was that Mr. Delic had helped a lot of people get released?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To be honest, I do not know. It is possible that he did. I was between Podorasac and Brdjani, my house and my late brother's house were a bit isolated. Maybe, probably yes, I do not want to deny that, but I do not know. I simply did not hear that myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Okay, that is fine, sir. Your Honour, I will pass the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Any further cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: May it please the court?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, you may proceed. Cross-examined by MS. McMURREY

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Dobardan, Mr. Draganic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My name is Cynthia McMurrey and I am Defence attorney for Esad Landzo. I know the Prosecution has already discussed this with you, but if we can have an agreement, I know Mr. Turone has prefaced most of his questions with "just tell us what you have personally seen and personally experienced" and I know that you have done that so far, but I want the agreement that you will only testify and give evidence in this court about what you personally saw; do we have an agreement on that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is what I am testifying to, only things that I saw myself. I am not saying anything that I did not see myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I want to go back a little bit to some things that Mr. Moran had asked you earlier, and I know you testified that at first you had not spoken -- first of all I want to go back. At your break just then, did you talk to anybody with the Office of the Prosecutor about your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean now? No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I mean when we had our lunch break.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Another thing you said earlier today was that you were invited by Ms. Mila Dordic of the Association of Detainees in Belgrade to Timosvara. You said that she found out about you by word of mouth by the friends that you had talked to; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These friends that you have talked to, when you were back in your home town and back in Konjic, in the Konjic area, you all talked about your experiences in Celebici, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Naturally, we talked about everything. We talked about things that we had gone through, things that we had experienced. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I think you said you were a construction worker and you said several times that you were -- I forgot the term you used, when you say that you did not work on site, you were out of the country on your work during that time before 1992? I know you were in Libya, but did you go other places to work also?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had worked in Iraq and all over Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said that when you came back in April 1992, you first came to Belgrade. Was that the place where the company that you worked for was located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I came back to Belgrade from Libya my sister-in-law was there and I spent a day there. I took a train in the evening, via Montenegro and Nevesinje, and I arrived to Borci, and there were some who had already left Konjic, and they told me not to go to the village because there was a war. I could not believe that that was true. I arrived to Bjela, my wife was from Bjela, she was staying with my father-in-law, and at that moment a man came from Konjic. He had his own fast food shop, he was of my age, I could not remember his name. He was looking for keys from a man named Boro Jakovljevic, and I asked him, "Can I go to Konjic with you?", and the man said, "Yes, you can", and naturally I went to his car, and there were already the green berets at the entrance to Konjic, and nobody really stopped me or asked me anything. I came to the exit from Konjic with him, to the post office. Then I hitchhiked, and a neighbour of mine, a Croat, named Juric Zvonko or something, I really do not know, I cannot remember, we used to call him Civala, he drove past with a Mercedes. He stopped, asked me if I wanted to go up. I said yes, so I went with him and I arrived home and there were no problems. That was 28th April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Draganic. I want to go back -- you said you went through Montenegro to Borci. Borci is the location outside of Konjic where the JNA had set up their shelling location, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also are good friends with Slobodan Zelenovic; he is from your village, is he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we have not even spoken at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In your village, there was an anti-aircraft gun that was brought in from Gorazde, is that correct, or do you know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That I do not know. I honestly do not know. I do not think it was there. Maybe it was, but I do not know about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am jumping around again. I want to go back to something you said earlier, that the lady from San Francisco in the United States, Desa Vokmen. When she called you, did she tell you how she got your name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: She told me that she had been informed by Nedeljko Draganic who had been a witness here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So she had spoken to Nedeljko Draganic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did she say whether she had spoken to him before or after he testified here in court?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: She did not tell me whether it was before or after. I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also stated earlier that you have talked to other people that have testified here. Who were those other people that you have spoken to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I spoke to Milenko, to Dragan Kuljanin, to those two people. Those are the ones I have spoken to, not with anybody else. They were the ones who were here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I did not understand which Kuljanin it was who you spoke to. Can you repeat that for me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dragan Kuljanin and Milenko Kuljanin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Milenko Kuljanin, is that Mici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you seen Mici Kuljanin since you have been here in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have. I have seen him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you discussed anything that has gone on in the courtroom with him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we did not talk about that at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now I want to go back to where I lift, since I am jumping around, we were talking about Borci a while ago. You said that you had gone through Borci to get back to your home. Can you just tell me the date that you arrived in Borci? I know it was in April, but April what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I arrived to Borci on 27th April in the morning, and when I arrived there to Borci, I had no transport and then in the morning, there were women leaving Borci for Konjic and I went with them and I reached Bjela. I arrived home on 28th April 1992, in the am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From Borci --

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I beg your pardon, sorry for interrupting. There is a matter for redaction and we should go to private session just to talk for one minute about that, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: May we go to private session, your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, let us go to private session. Let us hear what the subject matter is. (In closed session)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: (In open session)

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: May I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, you may.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Thank you. Going back to Borci again, I know how you got to your home town, but I would just like to ask, when you are in Borci, do you know how far it is from Borci to Konjic? Can you estimate what the distance is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the lake to Konjic it is actually 21 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. When you went through Borci, were you able to see or do you know what kind of JNA forces were organised there? Had they occupied the area? Did you see armed personnel carriers around?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Let me tell you, I did not see anything myself. The only thing was as I was leaving with these women at Vrapce, there were people, some were wearing military uniforms, some were wearing civilian clothing, but I really did not see any considerable military formations along the path that I took.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In your testimony earlier on Thursday, I believe you did state that it was a well known fact that everybody in Brdjani already had weapons; is that not true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is no secret, that was so, but nobody picked up the weapons. We all said that this would not happen, that a neighbour would not attack a neighbour, everybody would defend their homes, but things that were not supposed to happen, things that were not necessary, happened, but now it is too late and what is there is there. I have nothing else to say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One of the horrible things that happened that was not supposed to happen was your good friend, Agan Ramic, who you also worked with, he was one of the ones who harmed you most during this ordeal, did he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, and also I want to tell you that I am very sorry that that is so. I did not deserve that; neither I nor my late father, nor my late wife, nor my brother, nor my sister-in-law. He used to visit my home, I used to visit him. We used to have huts in the mountains. His parents used to go there. We used to visit each other. We were always good friends. I really do not know why that man bore such grudge against me. He took my car, he drove it away. All the things that he did, I really, as we say where I come from, halal, we do not mind, but he came to my home. He killed my father, my sister-in-law; that is inhumane. A normal person cannot do that. I lost four of my family members and I still have nothing against Muslims. I am not a nationalist. I love every human being provided it is a good human being. But what Agan did to me, I will never be able to forget or forgive that. I do not know why he did that. Fortunately I was not with my children at the time. My father saved them. He came to my home on 26th January in the evening. He said "Rajko, your mother came and told you, go to the village, take your children. I will stay with the in-laws". I did, I stayed in the village overnight. I went back and I saw the sight and I really do not understand how I preserved my state of mind. I have children left, I have lost my mother, I have lost so many relatives, I have lost my house, I saved my children. That really is tragic and I really do not know how to describe that to you. Just horrible. I did go to the village after that, in the morning, when I came, I had a friend who was a Croat, my neighbour, Ivica Petrovic, he was the director in the Monter company in Konjic. I went to his house in the morning, his wife had got up and she said; Rajko, do sit up, and I said; Maria, everybody has been killed in my home and Ivica got up, he had been with HVO. He got ready, the commission came --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am sorry, Mr. Draganic and I do want to express the concern and the condolences of everybody in this courtroom. I understand what kind of pain you have suffered, and not only with your friend Mr. Ramic, but also with your family and there is no way to explain what happens to people. Would a good explanation be that war turns people into other kinds of animals?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is true. That is so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This horrible fate that has befallen you is because a war was going on that you did not have anything to do with; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nothing whatsoever to do with it. I was not into politics in any way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to go back to Mr. Ramic. You surrendered your weapon to Agan Ramic, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was Agan Ramic, your good friend, that sent you to Celebici, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Maybe it was ordered from the other side, but he came to pick us up and he told us that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to go forward to your testimony about when you were placed in these manholes. I believe that your testimony was that you were able to breathe because the lids on this manhole did not fit tightly; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I do not know if the Prosecution exhibit is still over there, exhibit number 174, I think -- is that the one where you marked locations? Mr. Usher, would you please put that on the ELMO for me. (Handed). Can we see the whole picture? Yes. The first mark where you put number 1, the X over on the right side, I just want to make it clear, that was your position where you sat most of the time that you were in Celebici until right before you left at the end of August.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then you were moved to the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So over there, we see that Spaso Miljevic and Mirko Babic were pretty far away from you from that point, were they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but Mirko Babic was in the same row.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is what I wanted to clear up, too. The row that you have Mr. Miljevic in, is that row 1 or 2?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Row 2, Miljevic was in this row here (indicates).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that means that row 1 was up against the wall that the door is on, is that what we are saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we have row 1 which is on the wall where the door is, row 2 is where Miljevic is and row 3 is where Mirko Babic is. Then the fourth row is all the way across the back row; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I just wanted to make that clear.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Several times today and yesterday you talked about people being called out by Zenga. The truth is, Zenga did not come into the hangar most of the time, did he? You just heard a voice, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He entered all the time. He entered the hangar all the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But when people were called out of the hangar at night, you did not see the person calling, you just heard a voice, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There were a lot of young guards there at Celebici, were there not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You do not know the voices of all the young guards, do you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that he was the main torturer and he was involved in all the tortures and killings. I do not know who ordered him to do that, but he did all that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to go to your comments about Simo Jovanovic. You know that Mr. Jovanovic was a wealthy man from Celebici, was he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact he had some kind of fish farm, did he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he did. I heard about that. I did not see it, but that is what I heard. He was a manager in a construction company in Konjic or something.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know that when he was beaten in Celebici, his neighbours from Celebici were the ones who came into the camp and beat him, is that not right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. He was called out by Zenga, he was led out that night. Three days before that he was not beaten and then he was called out and that is when he died. I do not know who beat him but Zenga was the one who called him out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You also talked about Zeljko Klimenta. I know that Mr. Moran had already asked you a couple of questions about this guard named Padalovic, but you did know that Zeljko or Kelo or Mr. Klimenta was killed accidently, do you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is what was being said. Whether it was accidental or not I do not know, but that is what the story was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact you heard that that guard was crying when this happened, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see him cry, I saw that he was not in a very good mood, he was silent and he looked sad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I want to go to Mirko Babic too. You said earlier today that you personally saw Mirko Babic --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did see it. Because he sat in the same row where I was sitting, he was sitting here (indicates). I saw it when he beat him and then he set his trousers on fire. They were very thick trousers and they burnt well. The burn was caused and I do not know who put the fire out, but at any rate, there was a large wound in his lower leg.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if Mirko Babic testified in March that he was taken outside and that this incident occurred outside, he would be not telling the truth; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know, I think I am not mistaken because I was able to see that. He was taken out, but this is where he was set on fire. He was taken out on other occasions. This is what I saw. I do not know what he had said, but I am saying what I saw.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: (redacted) said that the knife was heated and placed on him outside the hangar near a shepherd, then he would not be telling the truth either, would he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. That is what I saw with my own eyes when he heated up the knife and when he was forced to hold it. This is what I saw with my own eyes. I do not know what the other people had said.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I just have one second? (Pause). Mr. Draganic, I want to, one more time, express our condolences for all the pain you suffered during this war. I thank you for your answers.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I am really grateful to this Tribunal for letting me tell you all of this, because I believe that there will be justice and that everybody deserves justice regardless of his or her religion or nation. Thank you. I think I will feel better now I have been able to tell you all about this.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I pass the witness, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: There is no questions for re-examination, your Honour, but I am sorry, there is another matter of redaction, so we have to enter into private session again, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Would you kindly go into closed session so that --

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Is this one which requires the witness to be present? (In closed session)

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: (In open session)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Mr. Turone, just a minute. While you were examining the witness, you took the names of these witnesses about what happened to him in his sight. The names that are already there, you want redaction on them also?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Our concern is that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Only the examination-in-chief or cross-examination also, because when you were asking the witness, "What did you see happening to that particular witness", you gave the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: No, the fact to be redacted is that a witness is mentioned as a witness. We never said that the given person was a witness in this room. This is the issue for which redaction is requested, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I suppose the problem is whether you refer to the name of this witness in the examination-in-chief. I did not hear it that way, but I do not know in what circumstances you might have referred to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: The circumstance is the fact that a given person gave testimony in this courtroom, not the fact itself that a given person was in the camp and was a victim. So we are requesting redaction only when it comes out that a given protected person gave evidence in this room, a given protected witness gave evidence in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: The risk of mentioning the name itself might make the person identifiable. That is a protection which the Tribunal is giving to a witness. The persons named should not be mentioned in connection with the trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Exactly, your Honour, not in connection with the fact that he was a witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: That leaves a danger of identifying the person within the trial, whether he was a witness or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I might just respond briefly, what happens is by them mentioning the name in direct and talking about the facts of the situation, and then by having us not able to mention the name in cross-examination, it limits us and hinders and effectively causes us to have infective cross-examination. They are able to mention the name because we cannot mention his prior testimony for impeachment and we are limited in our cross-examination. I think it is unfair to our clients, to the accused, to not be able to cross-examine after they have mentioned all of these facts and be able to compare them to his testimony that he gave in this court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I suppose you have a leeway in having a closed session and referring to it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: You are right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Referring to it in closed session.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: This is exactly what we intended, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I need to enlarge on that problem. If the Prosecution can elicit publicly information with regard to a particular individual and then we are required because we might want to refer to some prior testimony of that individual to do it all in closed session, what goes out in the public is then a lopsided story. I think the more proper way to do it would be if it is a person who was a protected witness in this court, then the Prosecutor also do their direct in closed session so that the lopsided nature of that does not appear out in the public as kind of an unfair reflection of what is going on in the courtroom. That is the problem, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I agree entirely with you. That was what I was getting across. If you know that a witness ought to be protected, do not mention the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: We will proceed in that way, your Honour, in future.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I think so. Can we have your witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. We call Milovan Kuljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Just a matter before the witness comes in. Mr. Niemann, today I got a list of the witnesses you intend to examine. That list has come out in the office and I do not know how far it would stand protected from the public. I was not interested in seeing the list but I still got a copy. It was lying on my table when I saw it. The list can come out. It is all over the Tribunal now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I was not aware that had happened to it your Honour. I will make enquiries to prevent it happening again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: We had a very heated debate a few months ago.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: -- can be dangerous in one sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I do not know how that happened, your Honour. I will find out. I need to make enquiries. (Witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Kindly swear the witness. MILOVAN KULJANIN (sworn)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You may sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you. Examined by MR. NIEMANN

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please state your full name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Milovan Kuljanin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have a nickname, a name that you are known by among your friends and associates?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you born?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the village of Blace, municipality of Konjic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 15th March 1970.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far did you go with your schooling?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I graduated from the high school for catering.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am orthodox.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the beginning of 1992, where were you living --

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: He answered his religion rather than his ethnic background.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Ask him whether he is a Croat, Serb or a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I will lead your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: There is no problem in leading in that sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I normally expect objections if I lead. Is your ethnic background Serbian?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the beginning of 1992, where were you living?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was living in Mostar until mid March, and then later I lived in Konjic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your employment at the beginning of 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was in the reserve forces of the Yugoslav National Army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that at Mostar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you employed prior to being in the reserve of the army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was serving, doing the national service in the Yugoslav People's Army in 1990 to 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. When did you leave Mostar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In mid March.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To Konjic, to my home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do then between March and the beginning of the war, the commencement of the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Around the beginning of June 1992, did you attempt to leave Konjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I just moved to Donje Selo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain what happened when you moved to Donje Selo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nothing -- well I went there for safety reasons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay in Donje Selo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Until I was arrested and taken to Celebici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who arrested you? How is it that you came about to be arrested? What were the circumstances of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can explain that. We were in Miro Golubovic's weekend house and Darko Verkic came to pick us up with 8 or 10 HVO policemen and then we were brought in for an interview to Celebici barracks, which was then the barracks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did Darko Verkic come to Donje Selo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was within his area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were you taken to Celebici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In a van, it was a Volkswagen van.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who took us to Celebici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I already said, it was Darko Verkic with his police officers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before you were taken to Celebici, did you have any weapons in your possession?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I had a pistol, a 7.62 calibre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did you obtain that from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was my private property.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apart from the pistol, did you have any other weapons at your disposal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were taken to the Celebici camp, what happened when you arrived there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We parked in front of building number 22 and we stayed there for about 5 or 10 minutes, I do not know exactly for how long and then we were moved to manholes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived at the camp, was there anybody there that you recognised?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, most of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us the names of the people that you recognised that you saw, that you recognised when you first arrived, that very first occasion when you arrived at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Muhamed Corovic, Esad Landzo, Edhem Jeliskovic, Edin Spago, and many others. Hazim Delic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see all of these people when you first arrived or did you see them, some of them then and then others later?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, then, when I arrived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you said a moment ago that you were then taken to a manhole; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but before that, when I had just arrived, I said that I was there in front of building number 22 for maybe about 10 minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anything happen to you when you were standing there in front of room number 22?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nothing special, but Ismet Hebibovic at one time came into the van in which we were and he started beating us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was he beating you with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He did not beat me. He tried to. Darko Verkic prevented that. He did not allow him to enter the van actually.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say you were taken to the manhole. Who took you to the manhole?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was Darko Verkic and Hazim Delic and a couple of other people, police officers whom I did not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where is the manhole in the camp that you were taken to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Where do you want me to show it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I am going to ask you to show it in a moment but I would like you to try and describe it generally for me first, if you would, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is maybe about 200 metres away from the reception building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like now to stand up if you would and walk around to the front of the model that there is in front of you and before you move, you will need to listen to my instructions because the moment you take your headphones off you will not understand me. When you move around to the front of the model, you may be given a headset with a longer extension over here, and I am going to ask you to point to where the manhole is in the camp, if you would. Can you move to the front?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Move right around to the front of the model. Just to start with, do you see the building that you first were near, that is building number 22, if you can see where that building is in relation to the camp, could you point to it? Take your time. Orient yourself properly so that you are familiar. First of all, does that model look familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I think this is the one, this one here (indicates).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you look at the model very closely. Can you tell me where you think the entrance to the camp is, where you enter the camp when you are brought into it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here (indicates).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to that entrance, are you able to indicate where it is that you recollect that the manholes were that you were taken to shortly after you arrived in the camp, to approximately the place where you think those manholes were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (indicates).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are going from one end of the model to the other end of the model. Just one more thing for me. You may not be able to see it, but the building, the medical centre building that was known as building number 22 that you referred to in your evidence, are you able to see where that is in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (indicates).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can go back to your seat. I have no further questions on that. When you arrived at the place where the manhole was, what happened? Can you explain what happened at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Hazim Delic opened the manhole and ordered us all to get in. Miro Golubovic entered the first and I followed him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apart from Miro Golubovic, was there anyone else other than him and you there at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not at that time. A while later maybe a couple of hours later, an older man was put in. I do not know who he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned Hazim Delic being one of the people that ordered you into the hole. Was there anyone there assisting Hazim Delic at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Darko Verkic was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe the manhole for us please that you were ordered to enter into? Firstly, can you give the court some ideas of the dimensions of this manhole?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 2.5 by 3 metres, I would say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 2.5 by 3 metres wide or high?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 2.5 high and maybe 2, 2.5 wide. I did not really take measurements.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the manhole go vertically down into the ground or did it go at a horizontal -- did it go horizontally into the ground?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was vertical. It was only half a metre above the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to determine what it is that you thought that the manhole was used for, what its purpose was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think these were intimidation methods.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want you to tell me what you thought it was used for before it was set up as a camp, before it was used to put you in, I want to know, were you able to ascertain --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understand. I think the manhole was used for controlling the reservoirs situating above the facility. Those were fuel reservoirs. The valves inside it I think were used for that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you entered the manhole, was there a lid or door upon the manhole?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was an iron lid on the manhole.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe this lid for us? How did it function?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was perhaps 80 by 80 centimetres. It opened to one side only. It had a padlock on the other side, a padlock to lock it up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it sealed or was there holes in it? Was it a sealed lid or were there ventilation holes in it at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was nothing on the lid itself, but in the corner of the manhole there was a pipe that was connected with the outside and that is how we got oxygen, through that pipe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you entered the manhole, which you have said in your evidence was vertical, how did you descend down into the manhole? How were you able to do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a metal ladder.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you were placed in the manhole, was the lid closed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether or not it was locked after you had entered?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it locked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Inside the manhole, what form of lighting was there, if any?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was nothing. It was dark.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe the air, the state of the air inside the manhole?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can only say that there was not enough air from time to time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What of the smell? Was there any smell inside the manhole that was distinctive?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, one could feel the smell of urine, because many people had already been there before me who had to urinate there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apart from Miro Golubovic, was there anyone else in the manhole when you entered it, or was it just you two that went down there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only the two of us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did Miro Golubovic stay in the manhole?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that day and maybe the night. I cannot really remember exactly, but he left before I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that another old gentleman who you could not recognise subsequently was put into the manhole. How long did he stay there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. He stayed behind. I do not know when he left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay in the manhole?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A day, a night and a day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe the circumstances of how it is that you managed to get out of the manhole?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I can. It was daylight, and the sun was very hot, that I remember because when they opened the lid of the manhole, I could hardly keep my eyes open. When I went outside I had a distorted vision of it, as if I was watching through a fog. I could not really see very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did this condition last?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My eyes?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did the condition with your eyes when you were suddenly met with the bright sunlight, how long did that affect your ideas for, approximately?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot say precisely, but I stayed down another minute or two in the manhole itself and only then, when ordered so by Hazim Delic, I left the manhole.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you left the manhole after being ordered to do so by Hazim Delic, was there anybody else there with him at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Pavo Mucic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you got out of the manhole, did anyone say or do anything to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was just ordered by Hazim Delic to enter the van, the IVECO van.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When Hazim Delic gave you that order, where was Mr. Mucic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the very manhole.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Mucic say anything to you at the time when you came out of the manhole?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What condition were you in when you came out of the manhole?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Helpless.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you were taken out of the manhole and ordered to enter the vehicle, where were you taken then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To building number 22.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was it that -- who was in the same vehicle that you were when you were taken towards vehicle number 22?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I said, Pavo Mucic and Hazim Delic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived at building number 22, what happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Horror. I was leaning against the wall of building 22, nobody asked me anything. I was beaten for half an hour without anybody even asking my name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who beat you? Did you recognise any of the people who beat you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to name the people that beat you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Edhem Jeliskovic, nicknamed Muf, Muhamed Corovic, Esad Landzo, Osman Dedic and others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were you beaten with on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With different objects, tool handles, electric wires, handles for shovels with different wires.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you with anybody else? Was anybody else with you at the same time you were being beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you happen to see the two persons, Mr. Mucic and Mr. Delic who had driven you to this spot during the course of this beating?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They went to the reception building across from building 22.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to see them in the reception building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I could not see them because I was facing the wall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just going back to the manhole for a moment, when you were in the manhole for the period of time that you were there, were you given any food or water?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you given food or water?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Following this beating that you were given beside room 22, what happened to you then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went for a formal interview, I think it took about half an hour, I cannot remember precisely. After that I was moved to building number 6.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The formal interview that you went to, where was that -- where did that interview take place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Opposite building 22.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you happen to know the name of the building that you were taken into for the interview?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who it was that conducted the interview of you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was Miro Stenek and Zovko, I do not know his full name. I know his nickname, it is Kuhar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to recall how long the interrogation lasted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Perhaps half an hour. I cannot tell precisely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the period of time that you were being interviewed, apart from yourself and Miro Stenek and Zovko that you have referred to, was there anybody else in the room at the same time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Hazim Delic entered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When he entered the room, did he have anything in his possession?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he usually had a stick with him, a baseball bat or similar object used for torture.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall whether or not he had any similar such objects with him on this specific occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to recall which of those objects it was on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a wooden object.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone strike you or hit you during the course of this interview?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, once.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who hit you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Hazim Delic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You then said that you were taken to building number 6. Do you remember approximately --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the date that it was that you were taken to building number 6, by any chance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was the second or third day after my arrival, so that would be the 9th or the 10th. I cannot remember precisely. It was five years ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what month it was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The month of June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe building number 6 that you were taken to? Are you able to give us a description of the building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course not. It was a building 25 metres long, 10 to 12 metres wide, used for warehousing transport vehicles of the former Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any windows in this building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Towards the top there was a small glass, just opening, not really a window.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I do not know if it is a translation error or what it is, but the transcript right now, the question was: "Are you able to give us a description of the building." The answer in English says "of course not" and then goes on to give a description of the building. Something is wrong, I do not know what it is. I do not know whether he claims he is describe it or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I think the fact that he is describing it may suggest that, but I will try and clarify it if I can. Unless the interpreters can assist us? Perhaps they may themselves realise it is a mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Return to the same question and then see how his reaction will be.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You can return to the same question and get his reaction to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Mr. Kuljanin, are you able to describe building number 6 that you were taken to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I am grateful to Mr. Ackerman for pointing that out. Were there any doors in building number 6?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were, a small door that we entered through and another large door that could only be opened if there was a need to open them for large vehicles, for trucks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your period of time in building number 6, was the large door opened very often?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the small door opened regularly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From time to time when needed, only if there was a need to go through it to go to the toilet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you first arrived in building number 6, were there already prisoners kept in that building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, over 250.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know any of the people that were kept in that building when you first arrived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Many of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know where those people that you knew had come from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to name some of the villages that you knew that some of those people had come from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those are mainly villages populated by Serbs, located in suburbian parts of Konjic such as Brdjani, Blace, Bradina, Donje Selo, Cerici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were the prisoners arranged inside the hangar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were seated one next to the other in rows.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember how many rows there were, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Five or six rows, sometimes four, because sometimes people left and the numbers decreased, the numbers of prisoners decreased.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you provided with any bedding inside the hangar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What arrangements were made for you to go to the toilet when you were in the hangar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We had a 20 litre bucket during the night where 250 of us had to relieve ourselves. During the day we would go outside. We had ten seconds.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went outside to go to the toilet, were you under guard or could you just go freely as you pleased?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were several guards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe the food that you were provided with during the time that you were in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was mainly just bread, rice and macaroni. At the very beginning, there were 18 people per 700 gramme loaf of bread, or 10 kilograms of rice per 250 people, just boiled in water.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the food that you were given sufficient to sustain your weight?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: By no means.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you lose any weight in the time that you were kept in Celebici camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, 43 kilograms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you seated inside hangar number 6?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I first arrived I was seated in the third row, perhaps five metres from the entrance, from the door and then two or three times I was moved during my stay until 9th December 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you first were seated near the door, were you able to look out through the door when it was opened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apart from being able to look out through the door, could you from time to time hear noises outside of the building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we could hear vehicles driving past, because the road was literally in front of building number 6.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apart from vehicles that may happen to have been driving past, were you able to hear other things outside of hangar number 6 other than vehicles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could hear only cries and screams of the people who were beaten, tortured there, right next to the hangar, by the door of the building, people who were taken out every day and every night, and beaten up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall some of the people who were taken out and beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course. About 150.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of the guards that took people out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to name any of the guards that took people out of the hangar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course. Osman Dedic, Esad Landzo, Eso Macic, Almir Padalovic, Muhamed Corovic and many others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the time that you were detained in hangar number 6, were you ever beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, several times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the beatings that you received all the same or were some more severe than others?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It would usually be the same thing, it would take about ten or fifteen minutes. I did not really count the blows.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you recall who it was that beat you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was beaten at the very beginning by Osman Dedic, Esad Landzo, Almir Padalovic and Muhamed Corovic, as well and many passersby who used to come there to vent their emotions out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were these men that you have just named, did they participate in one beating of you, or are you referring to a number of beatings that you received?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Every time I was beaten up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are there any particular serious beatings that you suffered that remain in your mind now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I think it was the first or the second day of my stay in building number 6, that is when I was beaten up the most. I was beaten for about an hour with different objects, with electric wires, with sticks, with wooden objects, with baseball bat. Anything that was handy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who beat you on this occasion shortly after you had arrived in building number 6?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I definitely know two, I do not know the others. I know that there was Osman Dedic and Esad Landzo. There were some locals from the village of Idbar, people whom I did not know personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Is that a convenient time, your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am not sure anyone else is noticing but it seems to me it is awfully warm in here. I do not think I am the only one that is noticing it. I am wondering whether maybe during the break someone can talk to the building people to get it cooled just a tad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. (4.00 pm) (A short break) (4.30 pm)

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Two people are standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I just take a moment to raise a matter very briefly? This is a matter which has been troubling me for some weeks now and it was finally raised directly at the beginning of this witness's testimony and I now think it is an appropriate time to raise it. I want to formally object to the Prosecutor at the beginning of the testimony of each witness asking a question which basically goes "tell us your ethnic identity". My purpose in making that objection is this: it is my understanding that the vast majority of the residents of the former Yugoslavia share the same ethnic identity, that being Southern Slav. What it is that separates them is their religion, whether they are Muslim or Orthodox or Catholic. It is a serious matter, and I think it is a serious matter for this reason. What caused the war was primarily the stirring up of nationalist identities, the stirring up of nationalist feeling, and it seems to me in a Tribunal, the stated purpose of which is to try to heal the nationalist fervour that was created during the war, that it is totally inappropriate for it to be perpetuated in this Trial Chamber by asking witnesses what their nationalist identity is under the guise of what their ethnic identity is. This witness is probably the first one who has answered it honestly, by saying, "I am an Orthodox". There is no ethnic identity, unless the witness happens to be maybe a Hungarian or an Albanian or something like that, who is not a Southern Slav, but these people are all Southern Slavs. That is their ethnicity. I think it just perpetuates the nationalist problems that created the war in the first place, so I think it is inappropriate for us to be doing it here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: May I say something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: It is the case of the Prosecution itself that these persons were taken to this detention camp just because they belonged to a particular ethnic group. In fact, when Dr Janine Calic was giving evidence I asked this question and she said exactly what you are saying now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I think before I call on the Prosecutor to answer, the last question you asked was the problem of the air conditioning, before we broke off, so when you stood up, I thought you wanted to hear our enquiry about it. We have made enquiries and I hear that there is some technical disfunction which is likely to be corrected by tomorrow morning. I do not know whether the Prosecutor should reply to this, but let us hear him. Whatever he says will be directed towards the presentation of his case. It might not be towards reconciliation of the parties, although there should be an aspect of our contribution to the whole exercise, but I think all the Prosecutor is doing is to present his case as neatly as he can do it. Let us hear you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honours. In fact I am surprised by this objection because I would have thought it was obvious that the classification of the group is essential for the Prosecution case and the protected persons under the Geneva Conventions.
