It is obvious that the differentiation between the groups is a matter that has to be proved and your Honour is quite right in what you have said, it also goes to the issue of persecution and the classification of the group that is attacked. All of those matters are tied up in the offences that the Prosecution are setting about to prove. One regrets that one has to pronounce or highlight that there is division in this tragic community, but sadly there is, but for the application of these laws to take effect, the proof of these matters is essential. In my submission, your Honours, this is necessary for the Prosecution to establish. When I am speaking of persecution, I am talking generally in terms of taking out a particular group of people and subjecting them to special treatment on the basis of their classification that the Prosecution is seeking to prove.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, not to argue, I just want to make sure I understand what he said. If I can boil it down and make sure that I am correct and if I am not, I sure want him to correct me, but it is the position of the Prosecutor that nationality as used within the definitions in the Geneva Convention is the same as religion or ethnic background, as it is used within, for instance, Article 4 of the Geneva Convention on civilians. Do I correctly understand him as saying that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I think we need not go into a long controversy about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do not. I just want to make sure I understood the Prosecutor's position. I do not think it is anything we need to fuss over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: As I said, he was merely presenting his case neatly as he intends to establish. Can we invite the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. Just before the witness comes back in, Judge Jan you asked me about the list of witnesses. I have made some enquiries about that. The position, as I understand it, is this, your Honour: that the list was drawn up and given to members of the Defence and at the request of your Honours' clerk, a copy of that was made available to each of your Honours. Only three copies were given to Mr. Hocking and we understood that they would receive no further circulation than merely from him to your Honours. It was not our -- we did not fear that under those circumstances, there would be a confidentiality risk. I guess in future we could perhaps write on the top that it is confidential which might solve that, but we did not fear that there was a concern having regard to the very limited circulation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your explanation. I regard them as confidential documents whenever such communications are made that is why my brother Jan has locked his up in his desk.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: I have taken that precaution.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. (Witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Please inform the witness he is still on his oath.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I remind you that you are still under oath.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Mr. Kuljanin, before the afternoon adjournment you were telling us about a beating that you were receiving shortly after you had first arrived in hangar number 6 and you had mentioned the names of some of the participants who were involved in that beating of you. You mentioned the name of Mr. Landzo. Do you recall if he struck you at all during the course of the beating?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also made reference to Mr. Delic. Were you struck by Mr. Delic --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Objection, your Honour. That is a misstatement of the evidence. He said Osman Dedic, as I recall the testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Osman Dedic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I do apologise, your Honour. Was Mr. Osman Dedic there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he strike you during the course of this beating?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, several times, just as Esad Landzo did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Esad Landzo say anything to you during the course of this beating?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He did not say anything. We were just beaten just like everybody else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "we were just beaten", was there anyone else there that you can recall was being beaten at the same time as you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was an elderly man, I think his name is Simo Jovanovic, and many others, Bosko Samoukovic and many others. There were five or six others while I was beaten on that occasion, but it was not outside. We were beaten one after the other. It was in front of building number 6.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You made reference to Mr. Esad Landzo. Did you know him by any nickname while you were in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, his nickname was Zenga.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you known him prior to going to the camp at Celebici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but I did not know him personally. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know of his family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew where he lived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was in my neighbourhood, the place was called Tjesanice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know any members of his family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I knew his brother.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what position he occupied in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think he was a guard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know approximately what age group he was? You do not need to be precise, but as your best estimate.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was five years younger than he is now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but do you know what age he was when he was in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe about 20, 19, 20.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you feel that you would be able to recognise him again if you saw him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the course of your evidence, you also made reference to Mr. Hazim Delic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you known him before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How was it that you knew him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, we lived -- he lived close by.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what he did for a living before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before the war, he had a kiosk where he sold cigarettes and newspapers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever have occasion to go to this kiosk yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, several times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what approximate age group he was during the time you were in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 30, 32, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what position he occupied in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot be exact, but I think he was the superior of the guards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you feel that you would be able to recognise him again if you saw him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the beginning of your evidence today, you made reference to Mr. Mucic in the camp. Did you know his first name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was Zdravko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know him by any nickname?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Pavo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you known him before you went to the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know any members of his family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, his brother. Two brothers, actually.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How well did you know his brothers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I just knew them. I knew that they were his brothers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know approximately what age group he was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well I cannot tell you exactly, but maybe 38, 40.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what position he had in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again I cannot be exact, but I think he was superior to everybody there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you feel that you would be able to recognise him again if you saw him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned earlier in your evidence that as soon as you were taken out of the manhole you were taken by vehicle down towards building number 22, and then after being beaten you were subsequently interrogated. During the course of this interrogation do you know whether or not a statement was taken from you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I gave a statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you write it down yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you given a chance to read this statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, by no means.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How often did you see Mr. Mucic in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, seldom compared to the others. He would visit from time to time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see him in hangar number 6?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that occasionally, just sometimes, or was it often?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just from time to time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the time that Mr. Mucic came into hangar number 6, can you recall whether or not there were any prisoners there who had any obvious signs of being injured?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was among them myself. Mr. Mucic came to see us all, he came to me and he asked me who had touched me. I could not tell him who had done that to me because I did not dare, because I thought I would not see the next day alive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who had touched you, in fact?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The day before Mr. Mucic's visit, I had been beaten twice. I was beaten -- I took the most severe beating by Esad Landzo, Osman Dedic, and two or three others whom I did not know from the village of Idbar near Celebici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did Mr. Mucic say to you when you said you did not know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nothing, they only stayed there for a couple of minutes, they did not stay long. Then they left from building number 6. 20 minutes later, Dr Relja Mrkajic came to examine me, and when he saw the state that I was in he went back to building number 22 and he talked to Mr. Pavo Mucic there, and then Pavo ordered me to be transferred to the infirmary; that is building number 22.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anything happen to you as a result of Mr. Mucic having you moved to building number 22?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I survived. I would not be here, that is for sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anybody criticise you or anyone hit you or harm you because you had been taken to room 22?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, on one occasion after about four or five days in the infirmary, Hazim Delic came in and he hit me over the legs with a baseball bat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he say anything to you when he hit you over the legs with a baseball bat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall a time when bullets were fired over your head in hangar number 6?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe this incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was in the middle of the day, Hazim Delic and Emir Delalic came through the door. Then Hazim Delic opened fire from an automatic rifle, and on that occasion the bullet that ricocheted, hit Davor Kuljanin in the head, wounding him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall an incident where you had bullets fired over your head, where you were specifically --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was in front of building number 6, not inside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe that incident for us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. It also happened during the day, I think it was in the afternoon. A group of about four or five people came.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you name any members of that group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can. Ratko Juric, Hazim Delic, Rajko Tomic, Pavo Mucic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened when this group came?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They took five or six of us out, they read the names from the list, and we stood outside the hangar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you facing the hangar or were you facing the group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were all standing opposite the hangar, not facing it. Then they asked which group we belonged to. I did not understand what it was all about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who asked this, who asked which group you belonged to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was Pavo and Hazim Delic, which groups we belonged to, because there were some groups in which prisoners were categorised.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Four or five of them went in and I remained out there alone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say four or five of them went in, are you referring to the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I mean the prisoners who had gone out together with me, they went back to building number 6.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I stayed alone and I was ordered by Hazim Delic to turn towards the hangar number 6, and a few seconds later I just heard four or five shots.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to tell who had fired the shots?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was turned backwards to it. I think the idea was to intimidate me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the shots were fired, who was in the group of men where the shots were fired from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were about five or six metres from me, and the group included Hazim Delic, Ratko Juric, Rajko Tomic and Pavo Mucic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How close to you -- were you able to tell how close to you the bullets were that were fired at you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot really say precisely, but not far.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the bullets fired above your head or to the side of your head? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the direction of my head.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see who in the group -- did you notice who in the group that it was that had guns?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All of them, but I think that it was Hazim Delic's automatic rifle that was used to fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why do you think that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because when I turned, I saw -- I judged by the reaction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone say anything to you after the bullets had been fired?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was just ordered to return to building number 6. I was ordered by Hazim Delic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Other than order you back, did anyone else say anything to you on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember when this incident occurred after you had arrived in the camp and were in hangar number 6?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot say precisely, but perhaps after a month, a month and a half of my stay in building number 6.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were in the camp, did you know a prisoner by the name of Simo Jovanovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had not known him personally, but I met him in the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anything happen to him while you were in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was beaten up several times when I was present.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who beat him up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, when I was beaten Simo Jovanovic was beaten as well, so that was two days after leaving the manhole. He was beaten by his next door neighbours, he was from the village of Idbar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And the other guards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know the names of any of the next door neighbours that beat him? Are you able to tell us those names?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know their names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know the names of any of the guards that beat him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, those were standard so to speak, the guards who were always there, but when Simo was beaten they came for that purpose, because two of them were there on guard duties for a few days, maybe even a month, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any of the guards that beat him people that you knew by their name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I knew Osman Dedic and Esad Landzo. Esad Macic as well, nicknamed Makaron, who was there in 80 per cent of the cases of beatings of detainees.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When Mr. Jovanovic was beaten, when you were in hangar number 6 did you see any of those beatings yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in the hangar itself. He received quite a number of blows.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When he was beaten inside the hangar, on the occasions that you saw this happen, did you recognise --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- the people that did these beatings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The people who were beating him, as I said, were locals. They were neighbours. There were two or three of them. Amongst them there were Osman Dedic and Esad Landzo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What ultimately happened to Simo Jovanovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Simo died, died due to beatings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know he died?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because I was moved to the infirmary and I was informed about this by my friends with whom I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, might we go now into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Can we go into private session now, please? (In closed session)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: (In open session)

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Mr. Kuljanin, the person that you have identified that we have referred to as witness N, is he a person that you knew in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, from building number 6. I knew him from building number 6.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you met him before? Had you met witness N before you had gone into the camp, or was he someone that you had met when you arrived there for the first time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had known him, but not enough.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the time that you were in hangar number 6, did you see anything happen to witness N?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I saw that several times. I saw that he was mistreated, tortured, beaten in many ways.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall now any of the people that mistreated him in many ways when you were in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were several of them, but Landzo Esad was there more than the others. He was the one who burnt and who hit with anything he could find.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to describe the incident -- no, I will withdraw that, your Honour. You mentioned a moment ago that he was burned. Did you actually see him being burned, or is that something that you were told about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see him on fire, but I saw him when he entered building number 6. He had a red tracksuit on him and there was still smoke coming out of it, so one could see that he was on fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him being taken out of hangar number 6 before he was burnt?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not once, he was taken out 100 times, same as I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the occasion that he was burnt, on that particular occasion, did you see who it was that took him out of the hangar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. They were called up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who it was that called him up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot say exactly because I did not see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When he returned to the hangar, and you say you saw that his trousers were on fire or had been smoking, were smoking from being on fire --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a red tracksuit, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see who brought him back?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One could see where it had been on fire. No, he entered alone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that apart from this incident where he was burnt, he was beaten on other occasions, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you actually see him being beaten yourself, or is this something that you were told?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw personally the occasion when he was beaten up in the hangar, in the hangar itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know who it was that beat him on this occasion inside the hangar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do and I do not. Most of them were passers-by who were beating up people from the list. They were simply given a list of people whom they were supposed to beat up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The people that you do know -- I am not asking you now who was beaten, I am talking about witness N. I am asking, did you know the people that actually beat witness N that you saw?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was usually Esad Landzo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When he was beaten, was anything said to him --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Actually, that was not what you asked. You asked him whether he knew the persons who beat him up. His answer "it was usually", that does not really mean the immediate person.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I will try again. You said that you had seen him being beaten inside the hangar. I asked you whether you had seen him beaten inside the hangar and you told me you did. I ask you: who was it that beat him inside the hangar? Did you recognise any of the people that beat him inside the hangar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I said that, it was Esad Landzo whom I recognised and Osman Dedic, and many of those who were there, passing by.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were in the camp did you know or come to know a person by the name of Zeljko Klimenta?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was sitting with me in the same row in building number 6.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you known him before you came to the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, much longer. About ten years before the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to say approximately what age he was?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the time that you were in the camp did you see something happen to Mr. Zeljko Klimenta?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Klimenta was killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see this yourself or was this something you were told about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I saw that myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe the incident as best you can remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can. I was sitting opposite the door. It was perhaps 8.00 in the morning, maybe even earlier. It was a very nice sunny day. He went out with Kujundzic, I do not know his first name, his nickname was Garo, there was Nenad Cecez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These people you have named, were they prisoners or guards in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes -- no, they were prisoners. At their request they asked the guard to go to the toilet, to go out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the name of the guard that they asked to go out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, his name is Almir Padalovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Go on. Tell us what happened.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Klimenta went outside in order to relieve himself. When he was in front of building number 6, five or six metres in front of the building itself, as he started walking towards the ditch where we used to relieve ourselves, Padalovic fired 7.62 semi-automatic rifle. He was about 20 metres away from him. He hit Mr. Klimenta in the back of his head, so he was killed on the spot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to say from what you were able to see whether or not this incident appeared to be an accident or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not think it was an accident.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why do you not think it was an accident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because he hit him precisely in the middle of the head.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you say -- I withdraw that. Your Honours, I have another matter that I would like to raise very briefly in closed session, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Can we kindly go into closed session, please. (In closed session)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: (In open session)

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you know Witness M before you went to the camp at Celebici? Had you known him or known of him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: During the time you were in the camp, did you notice anything unusual happen to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can say that Mr. M also had serious problems caused by Esad Landzo, because he inflicted burns on his hands and wounds by blows on his ribs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this something that you yourself saw or was it something you were told about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw myself when he was beating him inside building number 6 on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say he was beating him, are you able to say who he is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I said already, Esad Landzo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did this happen on just one occasion, or were there a number of occasions when you saw him beaten by Mr. Landzo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On several occasions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned a moment ago about him being beaten --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not just -- I apologise, but not just Esad Landzo, although many others who were there, such as Osman Dedic and Hazim Delic and all the others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned a moment ago him being burnt with a knife. Is that something you saw yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I could not see that myself because I was inside the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what it is that you did see in relation to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw it afterwards, after he had entered, I saw burns on his hands.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see who it was that called him out of the hangar before he was burnt?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was Esad Landzo, the guard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why was it that you were able to see Esad Landzo do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because he came to the door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When Witness M was returned to the hangar after -- when Witness M was returned to the hangar when you saw that hands were burnt, did you see who brought him back, if anyone did?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He came alone. Nobody brought him back. He walked in alone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you yourself see his hands?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I saw that when we were going out, when we were going to the toilet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Burns on his hands.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether or not Witness M received any medical attention for these burns?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see that. I did not see him receive it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have sought a redaction. If it is necessary for me to go into detail, I would ask that we go into private session so that I can ask that the redaction be effected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Let us go into closed session. (In closed session)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: (In open session)

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone please, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I think that should be the end of the day. We will continue tomorrow morning where you stopped. (5.30 pm) (Court adjourned until 10.00 am the following day) 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
